text: I went to a female dentist for a tooth extraction. I told her my blood pressure was normal, but it would be very high during dental procedures, making it impossible to extract the tooth. Even at the clinic, it was still high. I asked if I could have the tooth extracted after consulting an internal medicine doctor and having my blood pressure lowered. The female dentist replied that I should wait a month or two for my blood pressure to stabilize. I felt this was heartless; making someone with tooth pain wait 1-2 months. I then consulted an internal medicine doctor at Aemorn Clinic, who said that if the internal medicine doctor could prescribe blood pressure medication, the tooth could be extracted. The internal medicine doctor there said my case was similar to theirs (they were afraid of the doctor in the lab coat!), and they gave me medication to take two hours before the extraction. I want to share this experience as a cautionary tale about female dentists who make people wait 1-2 months. I went to Aemorn Clinic because a colleague recommended it. I told my colleague that the female dentist gave very poor advice and only offered a refusal. I definitely wouldn't recommend her to anyone.
